parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the project as an implementation of the upstream-compatible parse 1.20.2 API with parse, search, findall, compile, with_pattern, converter helpers, packaging, README, license, dotfiles, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation, file placement, packaging, and final delivery ownership. It used six verifier subagents only after the implementation and local tests were already in place, giving each a distinct read-only scope.
parallel.implementation: The parent downloaded the parse 1.20.2 source distribution, copied parse.py, pyproject.toml, LICENSE, README.rst, and tests into /workspace, then wrote .gitignore and .pytest.ini after upstream .gitignore was unavailable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was a single-module library, so integration was primarily file placement and packaging metadata. The artifact contained the required top-level project files plus tests and generated install/test byproducts.
parallel.verification: The parent ran the full reference pytest suite with 96 passed and 1 skipped, launched six read-only verifier children, consumed their aggregate reports, and ran a final isolated pip install and quickstart smoke check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure remained. Several verifier children noted prompt prose examples inconsistent with upstream parse semantics, but the parent treated those as spec prose mismatches rather than implementation defects and the official evaluator passed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same upstream parse 1.20.2 target, including the public API functions, parse.py entry point, pyproject packaging, README, license, and support dotfiles.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned the whole pipeline: reference acquisition, file creation, packaging setup, smoke tests, reference test execution, cleanup, and final response.
serial.implementation: The actor downloaded parse 1.20.2 wheel and sdist artifacts, extracted source, copied parse.py, LICENSE, and README.rst, and wrote pyproject.toml, .pytest.ini, .gitignore, and .git-blame-ignore-revs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final serial workspace was cleaned to top-level source and metadata files; it did not leave a tests directory in the delivered tree, but the package itself installed and passed the official tests.
serial.verification: The serial actor installed the package, smoke-tested key examples, copied the reference tests to a temporary directory, and ran pytest with 96 passed and 1 skipped.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure remained. The serial final response noted that no submit tool was available and relied on local equivalent test execution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel covered the required parse API, conversion system, pyproject packaging, README, license, dotfiles, and examples/tests by copying the upstream 1.20.2 source and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial covered the same core library and packaging requirements, but its final artifact list shows only top-level files after cleanup, not the copied reference tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized and satisfied the evaluator-relevant API and packaging requirements; parallel retained tests in the artifact while serial validated with temp tests but did not deliver them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel kept implementation with the parent and delegated six read-only verification scopes through AgentSwarm after the main implementation passed tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main actor with a todo list to create the project, install/test it, and close without any delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed verification but not implementation; serial had no cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were explicit read-only verification tasks with separate scopes, and the parent received the aggregate verifier result before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child briefs or inter-agent contracts; all context remained in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced verifier handoff boundaries, but they were not implementation interfaces and did not create unresolved conflicts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel downloaded the official parse 1.20.2 sdist and copied parse.py, pyproject.toml, LICENSE, README.rst, and tests into /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial downloaded wheel and sdist artifacts, extracted source, copied parse.py, LICENSE, and README.rst, and wrote packaging/config files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used a reference-package implementation path rather than hand-rolling the parser; parallel copied the test suite into the workspace while serial used it from a temp directory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for all six verifier children, received the aggregate AgentSwarm result, and then performed a final installation smoke check before its response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it sequentially inspected command results and continued through install, tests, final listing, and response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had additional child-result reception and adjudication work; serial avoided that lifecycle entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel writes to /workspace were performed by the parent; verifier children were instructed read-only, while packaging checks wrote only temporary install locations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one writer and later cleaned build, egg-info, and pycache artifacts, leaving a compact final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left more ancillary files in the official artifact, including tests and build metadata, but there is no evidence of conflicting concurrent workspace writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran pytest with 96 passed and 1 skipped, consumed the verifier swarm reports, then performed a final clean install smoke check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial smoke-tested the installed package and ran the same 96-passing reference test suite from a temporary test directory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed evaluator-aligned verification; parallel added redundant verifier coverage, while serial relied on direct local checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and tokens because of the six verifier children, but it did not time out and still completed the implementation, verification, and final check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with fewer tool calls and no subagents, closing after cleanup and a final explanatory response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra verification fan-out increased cost but did not displace required work or shorten closure enough to cause an adverse result.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status evaluations passed 96 of 96 tests. Parallel solved the task by copying the upstream parse 1.20.2 source, preserving tests, running pytest, and adding a verifier swarm before a final install check. Serial solved it by downloading the same reference artifacts, writing the package files, smoke-testing, running the reference tests from a temp directory, cleaning generated artifacts, and finalizing without delegation.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation and packaging from the parse 1.20.2 sdist.
Local pytest pass before verifier fan-out and final install smoke check after verifier return.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation from the same parse 1.20.2 reference artifacts.
Smoke checks and reference pytest run before final cleanup and response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel left tests and generated build/install metadata in the artifact, while serial cleaned down to top-level source and metadata files.
Several prompt examples conflicted with upstream parse semantics; both attempts followed upstream behavior, and the official evaluator accepted that behavior.
evaluator_effects: The official tests passed both solutions despite prompt prose examples that verifier children identified as inconsistent with upstream parse 1.20.2 semantics.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences describe strategy rather than a failure cause

candidates.reason: The parallel parent owned and completed the implementation by copying the parse.py reference source; children were verifiers, not unowned implementers.
No separately implemented components needed cross-agent reconciliation; the parent placed a single-module implementation and owned integration.
The parent assembled the required workspace files, ran packaging checks, and delivered; assembly was not left without an owner.
The parent controlled the end-to-end transition from acquisition to file placement, tests, verifier fan-out, final install check, and response.
The initial environment check and source download did not block productive work behind a harmful serial gate; implementation and tests completed successfully.
The verifier swarm occurred after implementation and a passing pytest run, not as an investigation phase that deferred implementation into a deadline problem.
No indispensable implementation or correction path was starved; the parent completed implementation and tests before launching verifier children.
The six-child fan-out increased time and tokens but did not exhaust budget, cause timeout, or displace required delivery or verification.
Each child had a bounded read-only verification scope and all children returned; no oversized child left indispensable work unfinished.
The executed child briefs specified read-only verification and concrete checklists; no known child requirement omission made work unusable or caused rework.
No children owned interoperating implementation components, so there was no omitted cross-agent file, namespace, input, output, or compatibility contract.
There is no evidence that a known finding or constraint disappeared between actors; the parent received the aggregate verifier result.
The verifier aggregate was large, but the parent consumed its substance and performed a final install check; no dependent action was left unfinished.
No verifier result described a superseded workspace state that the parent then acted on incorrectly.
Verifier reports identified prompt prose mismatches against upstream behavior, but the parent adjudicated them and did not leave incompatible reports unresolved.
The parent accepted completion after a passing pytest run, returned verifier reports, and a final install smoke check; no visible integrated gap remained unsupported.
The parallel run had no replacement or retry episode that repeated prior work without inherited findings or checkpoint state.

candidates.reason: All six verifier children completed and returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate; no active child was cancelled before needed work finalized.
The deliverable was already placed, tested, and finally install-checked before closure; there was no complete candidate left unpromoted in time.
No child implementation was merged after verification; the children were read-only verifiers, and the parent ran final checks after their return.
No delegated implementation was completed by a child and then left unretrieved; implementation was parent-owned from the start.
The verifier children returned in the AgentSwarm aggregate, and the parent proceeded after receiving that result.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; reported check mismatches were adjudicated as upstream/spec prose issues rather than abandoned work.
The parent explicitly consumed the completed verifier aggregate and used it to state that mismatches were prompt issues before final checking.
The run did not wait to timeout or near-deadline without inspection; it completed normally and inspected the returned AgentSwarm result.
Verifier children did not write implementation paths, and no concurrent agents claimed overlapping behavior or build ownership.
Only the parent wrote workspace files; no two live agents edited the same source or configuration file.
No non-entry source owned by another live agent was replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewritten by the parent or a child.
The parent copied the entry-point parse.py before read-only verification; no child or concurrent owner overwrote the required deliverable.
No broad parallel cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Although children shared the workspace for reading, the parent was the only workspace writer and no unstable state or provenance problem resulted.
No temporary artifact, cache, helper, or child-generated implementation was consumed as authoritative input by another actor in a way that contaminated verification or delivery.
